newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end lower, index tumbles 2.8 percent.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end lower, index tumbles 2.8 percent.

text.p: Bombay shares tumbled nearly three percent on Monday as speculators -- who were bidders after a business-friendly budget announced last month -- unwound long positions, traders said.

The benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index tumbled 110.27 points, or 2.84 percent, to close at a provisional 3765.77. On the National bourse, the index slid 52.10 points, or 4.6 percent, to finish at a provisional 1075.15
Traders said the euphoria of last month's federal budget -- which drove shares 16 percent higher -- was settling as foreign funds stayed on the sidelines.
"Speculative positions are being unwound. Most foreign funds seem to be waiting for prices to fall," said a chief dealer at a foreign brokerage.
Carry forward rates released on Saturday rose sharply to around 3.5 percent from 2.5 percent a week earlier, reflecting large overbought positions.
"High carry forward rates have dampened the rally," the chief dealer said.
"We think funds are likely to enter at around 3700-3750 levels. The market is cooling off and it will give people a chance to step in."

Shares on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) closed lower than on the BSE ahead of the last day of the current account on Tuesday. The National bourse index slid 52.10 points, or 4.62 percent, to close at a provisional 1075.15.
Independent Bombay-based think tank Centre for Monitoring the Indian Economy (CMIE) said in its latest report there are no clear indications that the economy has reversed its recent slow down.
"The most recent set of numbers neither deny the recovery in the growth in industrial production nor do they convincingly affirm," CMIE said in its February review of the Indian economy.

It said industrial production grew by 6.1 percent in the first quarter of financial 1996/97 (April-March) and 2.7 percent in the second quarter. The third quarter ended with an estimated growth of 3.4 percent, it said.
Aluminium shares bucked the downtrend, as investors bought after the budget hiked aluminium import duties. NALCO rose 1.75 rupees to 46.25 and Hindalco rose 23.50 rupees to 949.
